subject: Arabic
source: Drive: Curriculum/Arabic folder and Secondary Lesson Plan - Arabic - Y8 (format and approach); National Curriculum early language learning

lessons.title: This is a book: haadhaa and haadhihi
objectives: Say 'haadhaa' for masculine and 'haadhihi' for feminine things
Name four classroom objects in Arabic
starter: Say 'This is my father' in Arabic.
Say 'This is my mother' in Arabic.

teach.heading: Bismillah and our classroom
teach.note: Start with bismillah. Hold up a book and a pen to the camera and say the Arabic. Mention that the first word revealed in the Qur'an is 'Iqra' (read) - Surah al-Alaq 96:1 - to link to books and learning, in simple terms. Pupils echo.

teach.heading: haadhaa: masculine
teach.note: Explain: Arabic words are either 'boy words' or 'girl words'. kitaab and qalam are boy words, so we say haadhaa. Pupils practise 'haadhaa kitaab' and 'haadhaa qalam' with actions. Misconception: thinking gender depends on the object's meaning - it is a grammatical group.

teach.heading: haadhihi: feminine
teach.note: Show mistara and haqeeba as girl words. Tell pupils many girl words end with a round letter ة (taa marbuta), pointing to the ending. This is a handy clue. Pupils say haadhihi mistara and haadhihi haqeeba.

teach.heading: Boy word or girl word?
bullets: Look for the ة at the end
teach.note: Show a table of two columns; pupils sort the four words. Ask: which one ends with the round ة? Remind that clue works for most but not all words; for now we only use words that follow the rule.

teach.heading: Say it in a sentence
teach.note: Pupils point to the object on screen or in their room and say the whole sentence. Give feedback on the haadhaa/haadhihi choice. Sentence stems on screen help SEND pupils.

practice: Teacher points to a book and a ruler; pupils say haadhaa kitaab / haadhihi mistara.
Pupils sort picture cards into 'haadhaa' and 'haadhihi' piles.
Hold up an object from your desk and say the correct sentence.
Say 'haadhaa qalam' and 'haadhihi haqeeba' to a partner.
independent: Draw four classroom objects and write the Arabic sentence under each.
Sort six words into haadhaa and haadhihi columns.
Tell your partner three 'This is a ...' sentences.
exit: Which word do we use for a pen: haadhaa or haadhihi?
Say 'This is a ruler' in Arabic.
lessons.homework: Find three objects at home and say 'haadhaa ...' or 'haadhihi ...' for each. Draw one.
lessons.send: SEND: picture cards with Arabic labels; colour code boy words blue and girl words pink. EAL: add home-language word beside each picture. Stretch: spot the ة ending and explain the rule to a partner.

lessons.title: More things in our classroom
objectives: Say five more classroom words in Arabic
Say 'This is a ...' with the correct word
Read the Arabic words with short vowels
starter: Say 'This is a book' in Arabic.
Say 'This is a ruler' in Arabic.
Is qalam a boy word or girl word?

teach.heading: Recap
teach.note: Quick recap with flashcards: show picture, pupils say full sentence. Correct haadhaa/haadhihi errors with a gentle repeat. Praise accuracy.

teach.heading: Chair and table
teach.note: Show a chair and a table. Ask which ends with ة (taawila). So: haadhaa kursee, haadhihi taawila. The 'ee' at the end of kursee is long. Pupils echo and clap syllables: kur-see, taa-wi-la.

teach.heading: Door and window
teach.note: Point to the real door and window (or use pictures). Stress the long 'aa' in baab and naafidha. Remind that naafidha ends with ة so it is a girl word.

teach.heading: The board
bullets: The doubled letter is pressed hard
teach.note: Introduce shadda (the little w-shape above a letter) as 'double sound'. Model sabbuura with a strong 'b'. Do not name rules beyond 'press hard'. Quick drill: pupils echo.

teach.heading: Sorting game
teach.note: Show a word; pupils respond with a gesture: raise the left hand for haadhaa and the right hand for haadhihi. Play five quick rounds.

practice: Echo the new words after the teacher: kursee, taawila, baab, naafidha, sabbuura.
Say the matching sentence for each picture.
Pupils take turns to point to an object in their room and say the sentence.
Play 'What's missing?': hide one picture card, pupils say which word is missing.
independent: Match pictures to Arabic words on a worksheet.
Write the correct word: هَذَا / هَذِهِ before each noun.
Draw your classroom and label five objects in Arabic.
exit: Say 'This is a chair' in Arabic.
lessons.homework: Label five objects in your home with paper labels in Arabic and send a photo.
lessons.send: SEND: limit to three new words and use real objects. EAL: provide a bilingual glossary. Stretch: find which of the five new words end in ة.

lessons.title: Animals: This is a cat
starter: Say 'This is a chair' in Arabic.
What do we use for a girl word: haadhaa or haadhihi?

teach.heading: Animals
teach.note: Show animal pictures and make the sound or actions. Pupils echo. Mention that qitta ends with a ة so it is a girl word. kalb and asad are boy words.

teach.heading: Big animals
teach.note: Recall the letters ج ح from earlier work (jamal and hisaan). Mime a trunk (feel), gallop (hisaan), a hump (jamal). Point out that all three are boy words.

teach.heading: This is an animal
teach.note: Practise the sentence frame with each picture. Show a picture and pupils say the sentence. Reward correct haadhaa/haadhihi use.

teach.heading: Kindness to animals
bullets: We must be kind to them
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ taught kindness to animals. A simple authentic point: a person was forgiven for giving water to a thirsty dog (Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim). Tell this briefly and sensitively. Ask: how can we be kind to animals?

teach.heading: Guess the animal
teach.note: Play charades: a pupil or teacher mimes the animal, class says the sentence with the right haadhaa/haadhihi. Keep turns brief so every pupil can take part.

practice: Teacher points to an object in the room; pupils say the correct Arabic sentence.
Say the six colour words in Arabic.
Match animal pictures to the Arabic words.
Pupils choose haadhaa or haadhihi for each animal.
Mime an animal for a partner to name in Arabic.
independent: Draw three animals and write haadhaa/haadhihi and the animal name.
Sort the six animals into boy words and girl words.
Say two sentences about animals to your partner.
exit: Is asad a boy word or a girl word?
lessons.homework: Tell someone at home about three animals in Arabic and draw your favourite one.
lessons.send: SEND: use toy animals or pictures; offer sentence frames. EAL: add home-language animal names. Stretch: add a colour, e.g. هَذَا كَلْبٌ أَسْوَدُ.

lessons.title: Asking questions: What is this?
objectives: Answer yes or no to a question

keywords.def: a word that starts a yes/no question

starter: Say 'This is a lion' in Arabic.
Say 'This is a cat' in Arabic.
Which animals are boy words: kalb or qitta?

teach.heading: Asking what it is
teach.note: Hold up an object (a pen). Ask 'maa haadhaa?' Elicit 'haadhaa qalam'. Use gestures: question mark in the air. Remind about boy/girl words, and use different objects for haadhaa and haadhihi.

teach.heading: Giving an answer
teach.note: Model dialogue with two name cards. Pupils repeat. Make a pairwork structure: A asks, B answers; swap roles.

teach.heading: Yes or no questions
teach.note: Explain hal is a sign that a yes/no question is coming. Show a dog picture and ask 'hal haadhaa kalb?' Pupils answer na'am. Then show a lion and ask the same; pupils answer 'laa, haadhaa asad'.

teach.heading: Listen and answer
teach.note: Play a fast-fire quiz using the picture cards from the last three lessons. Pupils answer aloud. Allow SEND pupils to answer with one word.

teach.heading: Polite conversation
teach.note: Pupils role-play: greet, ask, answer, thank. Remind them of adab: eye contact and a smile. Perform one pair demonstration, then all pairs practise in breakout rooms.

practice: Say the Arabic for six animals when you see the pictures.
Pick haadhaa or haadhihi: asad, qitta, kursee.
Ask your partner 'maa haadhaa?' about an object on camera.
Play 'yes or no': teacher asks a hal question; pupils answer na'am or laa.
independent: Write a mini-dialogue: question and answer for three pictures.
Draw an animal and write 'maa haadhaa?' with the answer.
Role-play a greeting and question dialogue with a partner.
exit: How do you ask 'What is this?' about a pen?
Answer in Arabic: هَلْ هَذِهِ قِطَّةٌ؟ (the picture shows a dog)
lessons.homework: Ask a family member three Arabic questions using maa haadhaa/haadhihi and hal.
lessons.send: SEND: use sentence strips for question and answer. EAL: pair with a buddy to practise. Stretch: add a colour in the answer, e.g. هَذَا قَلَمٌ أَحْمَرُ.
